newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka bans air conditioner use to save power.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka bans air conditioner use to save power.

text.p: Sri Lanka, struggling to avoid power outages after a drought reduced the country's hydropower reservoirs to dangerously low levels, on Saturday banned the use of grid electricity to run air conditioners.
President Chandrika Kumaratunga has issued a banning order under the country's emergency regulations and it takes effect immediately, a Power and Energy Ministry spokesman told Reuters.

Offenders risked having their electricity supply disconnected, the spokesman said. "This is basically to avoid power cuts. We can save substantial amounts of electricity by shutting off air conditioners," he added.
Individuals and businesses are allowed to operate air conditioners using their own generators, he said.
The daytime temperature in Colombo is currently around 35 centigrade (95 fahrenheit).

Sri Lanka, which relies on hydropower for nearly 80 percent of its electricity supplies, is experiencing a drought for a second year in a row. The rest of its electricity is supplied by thermal power plants.
Officials for the state power monopoly Ceylon Electricity Board told Reuters that reservoirs hold enough water for only 30 days' electricity generation.
The southwest monsoon, which usually brings enough rain to fill the reservoirs, is not due until May.
